claim_text: apply_bridge_day must recheck existing target-day rows inside its transaction. A stale default plan or second application must refuse unchanged. Only literal boolean True authorizes replacing existing target day; truthy non-booleans refuse. Other dates remain unchanged. Full input fingerprints, concurrent scheduler and mootdx partial flush are out of scope.

verified_subclaims.subclaim: apply_bridge_day rechecks existing target-day rows inside its transaction, before any write
verified_subclaims.evidence: Static: bridge_hithink_stock_daily.py L260 BEGIN TRANSACTION -> L262 _day_fingerprints -> L263 existing=before.get(td,(0,))[0] -> L264-265 refusal guard, all inside try with L290 ROLLBACK. Dynamic: test_stale_default_plan_refuses_and_preserves_rows passed (rows present at apply time are seen and refused).

verified_subclaims.subclaim: stale default plan (allow_replace_existing=False) refuses with BridgeRefused and leaves target-day and other-day rows byte-identical
second application of a default-policy plan after an authorized replace refuses and preserves the first apply's rows
only literal boolean True authorizes replacement; truthy non-booleans refuse unchanged
verified_subclaims.evidence: identity check `is not True` at L264; parametrized probe tests for 1, 'yes', [True]: 3/3 PASSED, rows unchanged in each

verified_subclaims.subclaim: plan without a policy key refuses unchanged (default-deny)
with literal True, replacement succeeds with correct reporting (deleted_replaced=1, written_rows=2, final_rows=2, other_days_unchanged is True)
verified_subclaims.evidence: control test: PASSED; target day shows exactly the new rows, old row gone

verified_subclaims.subclaim: other dates remain unchanged on both the refuse and the replace paths
verified_subclaims.evidence: other-day row (2026-09-21, 000001.SZ) asserted equal before/after in every probe test: 6/6 PASSED

not_verified_subclaims: True concurrent-writer isolation (racing scheduler interleaving): explicitly out of scope; staleness was simulated by pre-inserted rows on a single connection, which exercises the recheck logic but cannot prove DuckDB transaction-isolation behavior under concurrency
The internal drift/gone fingerprint guard (L277-283) was never triggered directly; only its end-to-end property (other-day row unchanged) was asserted
Rollback after a mid-transaction failure (e.g., final-count mismatch L284-287 after DELETE+INSERT) was not exercised; tested refusals all occur before any write

build_bridge_day's own gates (existing-row check L162-169, coverage MIN_COVERAGE, universe drift, preview_stock_calculation, real hithink fixtures): not exercised; plans were hand-built per claim scope
Empty-rows refusal (L256-257), name-resolution/turnover/source policy details, and policy=None (AttributeError instead of BridgeRefused, still rolled back): not exercised
Full input fingerprints, concurrent scheduler, mootdx partial flush: out of scope per claim

findings.trigger: hypothetical/static only: a write that altered exclusively non-fingerprinted columns (open/high/low/volume/pct_chg/stock_name) on a non-target day
findings.actual_result: the drift/gone guard would not fire, because the per-day fingerprint hashes only stock_ts_code, close, amount, pre_close plus row count
findings.impact_on_verdict: none — not triggerable via any path exercised by the claim; the probe verified other-day unchanged by exact row comparison, not by relying on the fingerprint

author_test_counts.note: author tests were withheld during probe design; executed afterwards in the same sandbox and agree with probe results

positive_control.detail: test_intentional_red_probe_bug asserts 1 == 2 and failed as designed ('intentional positive control: probe_bug'). This is an intentional red assertion in the probe harness, classified as probe_bug, NOT a product defect. It confirms the execution harness runs assertions and surfaces failures.

limitations: Staleness was simulated on a single connection (rows pre-inserted before apply); the recheck's placement inside the transaction is confirmed statically (L260 before L262-265) and behaviorally, but true concurrent interleaving is out of scope and untested
Tests cannot distinguish in-transaction from pre-transaction recheck on one connection; the static ordering evidence carries that part of the claim

The drift/gone guard's fingerprint covers count + hash(code, close, amount, pre_close) only; columns open/high/low/volume/pct_chg/stock_name are outside the other-days guard (informational, not exercised by any tested path)
Rollback correctness after a partially-applied write (post-DELETE failure) is untested; all tested refusals happen before any write

No production database was touched (sandbox denies production access); all evidence is from fresh :memory: DuckDB fixtures with hand-built plans; build_bridge_day, preview_stock_calculation, real hithink data, staging/atomic swap (run_daily_full_staged) are outside this claim and unreviewed
This verdict covers claim F3 only; it is not a full-repo review, not a production acceptance, and not a concurrency guarantee
scope_disclaimer: Verdict applies solely to claim F3 as scoped. No full-repository correctness, no production acceptance, and no concurrent-scheduler behavior is claimed.
